short: An effective but autocratic administrator whose growing terror of conspiracy ended in his own assassination.
full:
Domitian became emperor on 14 September 81 CE, the last of the Flavian brothers, and governed for fifteen years with more direct control than his father or brother had claimed, taking the censorship for life and insisting on formal address as lord and god. He secured the frontiers, reformed the currency, and expanded the bureaucracy, while conducting increasingly harsh treason trials against the senatorial class.

The trials fed on themselves: the more senators Domitian executed for conspiracy, the more reason the survivors had to conspire. He was stabbed to death in his own palace on 18 September 96 CE by a group including his own chamberlain, with the tacit knowledge of his wife. The Senate, delighted, condemned his memory and had his name erased from public inscriptions, and turned to the elderly senator Nerva to prevent another succession crisis.
